newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' 91-day T-bill rate up at 11.562 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' 91-day T-bill rate up at 11.562 pct.

text.p: The Philippines' benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rate inched up to 11.562 percent from 11.528 percent last week at the regular weekly auction on Monday, the Bureau of Treasury said.
The auction committee received 1.505 billion pesos worth of bids but accepted only 1.0 billion pesos for the three-month bills.
The average rate for the 182-day T-bills also rose to 12.197 percent from 12.05. A total of 1.635 billion pesos in tenders was received, but only 1.0 billion pesos worth were awarded.
The 364-day T-bills dipped to 12.610 percent from last week's 12.688 percent.
Financial institutions flocked to the one-year bills with total tenders of 5.255 billion pesos. The auction committee only accepted 1.5 billion pesos.
Traders said the uptick in the short-term bills was due to market expectations that October inflation, due out on Tuesday, will be slightly higher than last month's.
The rate decline in the one-year bills came after the committee cut down the size of its weekly offer to 1.5 billion pesos from 2.5 billion pesos.
